name: TSMC’s 193 nm immersion lithography
description: TSMC integrated 193 nm water-immersion lithography into semiconductor fabrication, testing it on 90 nm devices and later qualifying manufacturing processes that used it, including N45LP and the 40 nm variants.

date.basis: Date or date granularity stated in the cited source.

events.statement: TSMC demonstrated manufacturing feasibility by completing functional 90 nm SRAM with a critical layer exposed using an ASML immersion prototype.
events.caveats: The 90 nm result establishes feasibility on functional devices. TSMC announced it at the end of 2004. The trial does not establish volume manufacture via immersion on the 90 nm node.

evidence.supports: Documents the split dry/immersion wafer batch, ASML prototype exposure and TSMC’s completion of functional SRAM.

evidence.locator: §2 Business Overview, Innovation, and §5.2 R&D Accomplishments in 2004
evidence.supports: TSMC reports the 193 nm feasibility result and the use of ASML tools for functional 90 nm devices.

evidence.locator: Slides 17–18, Technology accomplishments 2004 and Immersion working on the fab floor
evidence.supports: ASML records early customer development shipments and a separate 90 nm microprocessor immersion result. The presentation does not identify the TSMC SRAM trial.

date.label: Q3 2007
date.basis: TSMC dates qualification and delivery of its low-power N45LP flavour to the third quarter.

events.statement: TSMC qualified and delivered its low-power 45 nm N45LP process with 193 nm immersion lithography.
events.scope: N45LP qualification and delivery. The source gives a separate later milestone for the broader 45 nm generation.

evidence.supports: Names the process, optical technique, and quarter of qualification and delivery.

date.label: Q4 2008
date.basis: TSMC dates qualification and delivery of the 40 nm variants using immersion to the fourth quarter.

events.statement: TSMC qualified and delivered both its 40 nm general-purpose and low-power technologies using 193 nm immersion lithography.
events.scope: TSMC’s two 40 nm variants. The October customer-wafer milestone does not narrow the qualification and delivery of both immersion processes from the documented quarter.

evidence.supports: Describes the 193 nm method and Q4 qualification and delivery of both 40 nm processes.

evidence.locator: Main paragraphs 1 and 9, TSMC 40nmG and 40nm LP
evidence.supports: Documents initial 40 nm customer wafers entering production in October, with the volume ramp announced by 17 November.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated result within the sampled sources is the 2004 90 nm feasibility demonstration.

research.note: The node covers TSMC’s integration of the technique. It leaves water-immersion priority and possible earlier practical use at other companies open.

links.statement: TSMC’s 90 nm SRAM trial used an early ASML immersion scanner to expose a critical layer before TSMC completed the wafers.
links.scope: ASML’s early TWINSCAN immersion scanner line as used in the 2004 feasibility trial.
links.caveats: TSMC’s release describes the prototype without a model or serial number. The link does not identify a particular scanner used in subsequent TSMC production.

evidence.supports: The foundry specifies the ASML prototype exposure and completion of SRAM at TSMC.
The supplier documents the early TWINSCAN prototype, follow-on scanner, and joint immersion programme with TSMC.
The supplier confirms that TSMC’s functional 90 nm chips used its early immersion equipment.
